PASS with caveat. The study ran TWO Qualtrics forms (S1 File): an obstetrician form and a pediatrician/NP form, and the IRW table pools both. 11 of the 16 items appear on the obstetrician form (live n 14-96, including obstetrician responses), 5 appear only on the pediatrician/NP form (live n 80-81, zero obstetrician responses); the per-item n reproduce the S2 workbook column counts 16/16. Of the 7 items asked on BOTH forms, 4 are worded slightly differently between them: 'usually_ask...first_visit' (obst: '...in their first visit'; ped: '...in their first visit with their infant (right after birth)'); 'if_noticed...' (obst: 'If I noticed the patient is looking sad...'; ped: 'If I noticed the mother looking sad...'); 'ask_about_the_mothers_connection...' (obst: '...during the postpartum office visits'; ped: '...during office visits'); 'ask_about_the_mothers_social_support...' (obst: '...and forms of help she has'; ped: '...and forms of help'). The shipped item_text is in each case the variant that the S2 workbook's own column name reproduces; the other variant is recorded here. The obstetrician form also carries a second, unused mother-infant-connection item (QID34) that has no column in the deposit. option_text ships the deposit's normalised lowercase value labels (never/sometimes/about half of the time/most of the time/always), which is what the IRW processing script maps to 1-5; the administered Qualtrics anchors vary cosmetically by item and form ('Most of the time' vs 'Most of the times', 'Sometime' vs 'Sometimes', and one item offers a stray 'Moderately unlikely' option nobody used). AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (orchestrator, Step 5c): audit_batch.R WARNs 'row-count anomaly (possible item-code conflation or missingness skew), median=81'. This is NOT an itemtext defect and NOT item-code conflation -- it is a property of the response data, namely the two-form design above. Orchestrator re-derived the live per-item n independently via item_stats.R: 15,15,81,96,96,14,80,96,81,95,94,15,81,96,96,81. Those fall into three clean strata -- 4 obstetrician-only items at n=14-15, 5 pediatrician/NP-only items at n=80-81, and 7 items asked on both forms at n=94-96 -- which is exactly the form membership the survey design implies, not skewed missingness within a single form. The four items the WARN names are simply the ones furthest from the median of a legitimately trimodal distribution. No action needed.
